questions.q: What is the key difference between EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE?
options: EXPLAIN ANALYZE actually runs the query and reports real timing and row counts, not just the planner's estimate
EXPLAIN ANALYZE only works on INSERT statements
There is no functional difference between them
EXPLAIN ANALYZE only shows the query text, not a plan
questions.explain: EXPLAIN alone reports the planned strategy without executing; EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes and adds actual time and rows to each plan node.

questions.q: What does a Seq Scan operator mean in a PostgreSQL plan?
options: A full table scan reading every row
A scan that only reads index pages
A scan guaranteed to use parallel workers
A scan that always indicates a performance bug
questions.explain: Seq Scan reads the entire table sequentially — appropriate for small tables or when most rows qualify, a concern on large tables when few rows match.

questions.q: In a Nested Loop plan node, what does a high 'loops' value on the inner scan indicate?
options: The inner scan executed once for each row produced by the outer side
The query failed and retried that many times
The table has that many indexes
PostgreSQL is running in parallel mode
questions.explain: In a Nested Loop, the inner side is probed once per outer row, so loops equals the outer row count.

questions.q: What does it mean when EXPLAIN ANALYZE's actual row count differs wildly from the cost estimate's row count, per this lesson?
options: The planner's statistics are likely stale or the estimate mispredicted, which is often the real cause behind a bad plan
The query returned corrupted data
PostgreSQL always shows a random estimate unrelated to reality
The table needs to be dropped and recreated
questions.explain: The lesson identifies this estimate-vs-actual mismatch as frequently the most useful diagnostic signal in the whole plan.

questions.q: What makes an Index Only Scan faster than a regular Index Scan?
options: Every column the query needs is already in the index, so the table itself is never touched
It skips using the index entirely
It only runs during EXPLAIN, not EXPLAIN ANALYZE
It always uses a Hash Join internally
questions.explain: An Index Only Scan avoids the extra step of fetching matching rows from the table because the index alone has everything the query needs.
